mainTopic: Dangers in drinking water (leeches, hornets, שברירי at night), and the new משנה about decorated shops in a city with עבודה זרה
overview: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא mentioned water-spouting פרצופות so it could add a related rule: don't drink straight from a pipe, because of danger. The danger is swallowing a leech (עלוקה), and a second ברייתא about drinking from rivers and ponds says the same. That backs up רבי חנינא, who allows heating water on שבת for someone who swallowed a leech, and a story with רבי נחמיה confirms it. While the water heats, the person should sip vinegar. רב אידי בר אבין adds that a swallowed hornet is deadly, but strong vinegar may buy time for final instructions. A ברייתא then warns against drinking water at night because of a spirit called שברירי, and gives remedies for a thirsty person. A new משנה rules that in a city with עבודה זרה, decorated shops are forbidden and plain ones permitted. ריש לקיש limits this to roses and myrtle, whose smell gives benefit, and starts bringing a פסוק as the source; the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why mention the water-spouting faces?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothered to list the case of פרצופות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the case of the faces?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier ברייתא needed to mention statues with faces that spout water. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had already taught a similar case about drinking near עבודה זרה, so the faces case seems to add nothing new. The גמרא assumes every case in a ברייתא must teach something, so it wants to know what this one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Faces: statues or fountains shaped like faces that spout water
Why do I need it? The standard way to ask why a case is mentioned at all

phrases.english: Why do I need the case of the faces?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא a few lines up about faces that spout water, where drinking from them looks like kissing the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by asking about a case in the earlier ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the פרצופות case add that the ברייתא had not already taught?

steps.title: It leads into the rule about drinking from a pipe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentioned the faces so it could go on to teach a related rule: don't drink straight from a pipe, because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the ברייתא wanted to go on and teach: 'In the same way, a person should not put his mouth on a pipe and drink, because of the danger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the faces case was mentioned so the ברייתא could add a similar rule about drinking from a pipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The faces case connects to the new rule, because both involve putting your mouth on flowing water. The new rule has nothing to do with עבודה זרה. It is about physical danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it wanted to teach: the case was included to lead into another teaching
A pipe or spout that water flows through

phrases.english: Because it wanted to teach:
Similarly, one should not place his mouth
on a pipe and drink,
because of the danger.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The faces case is there to introduce the next rule: don't drink directly from a pipe because of danger.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. The faces case is about looking like you are kissing an idol. The pipe rule is about danger to your health.

steps.title: What is the danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what danger the ברייתא means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what danger there could be in drinking from a pipe. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said 'because of the danger' without explaining it. The גמרא wants to know exactly what the danger is.

phrases.english: What danger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word 'danger' in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the specific danger of drinking from a pipe?

steps.title: The danger is a leech
steps.stepSummary: The danger is swallowing a leech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the danger is swallowing a leech that could be in the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you drink straight from a pipe, you can't see what is going into your mouth. A leech could slip in and get swallowed.

phrases.english: A leech.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The danger is swallowing a leech.

steps.title: A ברייתא about drinking from rivers and ponds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא warns against drinking from rivers or ponds with your mouth or one hand, and explains that the danger is a leech.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person should not drink water from rivers or ponds, either with his mouth or with one hand. If he does drink that way, his blood is on his own head, because of the danger. What danger? The danger of a leech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that also says the danger in drinking water carelessly is swallowing a leech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא names leeches as a danger of drinking water, which supports the answer in step 4. Drinking with your mouth or with one hand gives you no chance to see what is in the water. 'His blood is on his head' means he is responsible for whatever harm comes to him.

keyTerms.meaning: His blood is on his head: he is responsible for his own harm

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A person should not drink water

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִן הַנְּהָרוֹת וְלֹא מִן הָאֲגַמִּים,
phrases.english: not from rivers and not from ponds,
not with his mouth and not with one hand,
and if he drank, his blood is upon his head,
because of the danger.
What danger? The danger of a leech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that also names the leech as the danger
steps.raayaObject: That the danger of drinking water carelessly is swallowing a leech
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about drinking from rivers and ponds
steps.whatToRemember: Drinking straight from a pipe, or from a river with your mouth or one hand, is forbidden because you might swallow a leech.

steps.title: Support for רבי חנינא: heating water on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports רבי חנינא, who rules that we may heat water on שבת for someone who swallowed a leech.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי חנינא, because רבי חנינא said: Someone who swallowed a water leech, it is permitted to heat hot water for him on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא backs up רבי חנינא's ruling that swallowing a leech is a life-threatening danger, serious enough to break שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls a leech a real 'danger', and רבי חנינא treats it as a matter of life and death (פיקוח נפש). That is why he allows heating water on שבת, which is normally forbidden work. The ברייתא's serious language supports his ruling.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Ḥanina,
as Rabbi Ḥanina said:
One who swallows a water leech,
it is permitted to heat hot water for him on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 5 to support a ruling of רבי חנינא
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's ruling that swallowing a leech is dangerous enough to break שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in step 5, which calls the leech a danger
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that swallowing a leech counts as פיקוח נפש, so שבת rules are set aside to help.

steps.title: The story with רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: A real case: someone swallowed a leech, and רבי נחמיה allowed heating water for him on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a case of someone who swallowed a water leech, and רבי נחמיה allowed them to heat hot water for him on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רבי נחמיה actually ruled this way in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story (מעשה) shows the rule being used in real life. רבי נחמיה's ruling matches רבי חנינא's statement exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident that really happened

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבָּלַע נִימָא שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: And there was an incident with one who swallowed a water leech,
and Rabbi Neḥemya permitted
to heat hot water for him on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבָּלַע נִימָא שֶׁל מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that matches רבי חנינא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: That heating water on שבת for one who swallowed a leech is allowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical ruling by רבי נחמיה

steps.title: What should he do while waiting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the person should do until the hot water is ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the meantime, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the person should do while he waits for the water to heat up. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating water takes time, and the leech is dangerous right now. So the גמרא asks for an immediate step to take.

keyTerms.meaning: In the meantime, while this is happening

phrases.english: In the meantime?
phrases.notes: The question is that short. He's asking: until the water is hot, what should the person do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a practical follow-up to the ruling about hot water
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What should the person do right away, before the hot water is ready?

steps.title: Drink vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the person should sip vinegar in the meantime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: He should swallow vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the person should drink vinegar while waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is ready right away and needs no work on שבת. It is meant to help until the hot water is ready.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
He should swallow vinegar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drink vinegar until the hot water is ready.

steps.title: Someone who swallowed a hornet
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says someone who swallowed a hornet will not survive, but strong vinegar may keep him alive long enough to give final instructions to his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: Someone who swallowed a hornet will not live. But they should give him a רביעית of strong vinegar to drink. Maybe he will live a little while, long enough to give instructions to his household.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין adds a related teaching about swallowing a hornet, which is even more dangerous than swallowing a leech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the leech, a swallowed hornet is deadly. Vinegar can't save him, but strong vinegar may buy him time. That time lets him tell his family his final wishes.

keyTerms.meaning: A רביעית, a quarter of a לוג (a small measure)
He gives instructions to his household (his final wishes)

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
One who swallowed a hornet,
will not live,
but they should give him a quarter-log of sharp vinegar to drink,
it is possible that he will live a little
until he can instruct his household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case about swallowing something dangerous, also treated with vinegar
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A swallowed hornet is fatal, but a רביעית of strong vinegar may give the person enough time to give his family final instructions.
steps.whatToRemember: Leech: heat water even on שבת, and give vinegar in the meantime. Hornet: deadly, but strong vinegar may buy time for final instructions.

steps.title: Do not drink water at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person should not drink water at night because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person should not drink water at night. If he does, he is responsible for what happens to him, because it is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new health warning: do not drink water at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the last steps, which dealt with dangers to the body. The ברייתא says there is a danger but does not yet say what it is. That sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: His blood is on his own head. He alone is responsible for the harm.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם מַיִם בַּלַּיְלָה,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: A person should not drink water at night,
and if he drank, his blood is on his own head,
because of the danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם מַיִם בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of health dangers, like the leech and the hornet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not drink water at night. It is dangerous.

steps.title: What is the danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which danger the ברייתא means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to explain the ברייתא: which danger does it mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said "the danger" and did not explain it. The גמרא wants to know exactly what is risky about drinking water at night.

phrases.english: What is the danger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the word "danger" in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of danger comes from drinking water at night

steps.title: The danger of שברירי
steps.stepSummary: The danger comes from שברירי, a harmful spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the danger is from שברירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is not from the water itself. It comes from a harmful spirit called שברירי, which is connected to water at night.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a harmful spirit connected to water at night

phrases.english: The danger of shavrirei.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The danger is the harmful spirit שברירי.

steps.title: What if he is thirsty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person can do if he is thirsty at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is thirsty, what is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: if someone is thirsty at night, how can he drink safely? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being told "never drink at night" is hard for a thirsty person. So the גמרא looks for a safe way to drink.

phrases.english: And if he is thirsty, what is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming the danger, the גמרא asks for a way to protect against it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a thirsty person can safely drink at night

steps.title: Wake a friend, or say a protective formula
steps.stepSummary: If someone else is there, wake him and tell him you are thirsty. If not, tap the jug lid and say a special formula against שברירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone else is with him, he should wake him and say, "I am thirsty for water." If not, he should knock the lid on the jug and say to himself: "So-and-so son of so-and-so, your mother told you to beware of שברירי, ברירי, רירי, ירי, רי, in white cups."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two remedies: one for a person who is with someone, and one for a person who is alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a friend, simply waking him and saying out loud that you are thirsty is enough. Alone, he knocks the lid on the jug and says a formula that names the spirit. Each time he repeats the name, it gets shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so son of so-and-so. He puts in his own name and his mother's name.

steps.whatToRemember: Drinking water at night is dangerous because of שברירי. A thirsty person should wake a friend, or if alone, tap the jug and say the protective formula.

phrases.english: If there is another person with him,
he should wake him and say to him:
"I am thirsty for water,"
and if not,
he should knock with the lid on the jug,
and say to himself:
"So-and-so son of so-and-so,
your mother told you

phrases.aramaic: אִזְדְּהַר מִשַּׁבְרִירֵי בְּרִירֵי רִירֵי יְרֵי רֵי
phrases.english: beware of shavrirei, verirei, rirei, yirei, rei
in white cups."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and closes the health-danger section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wake a companion and say you are thirsty. If alone, knock the lid on the jug and say the formula against שברירי.

steps.title: New משנה: decorated shops in a city with עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: In a city with עבודה זרה, the חכמים ruled in בית שאן that decorated shops are forbidden and plain shops are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A city that has עבודה זרה, with some shops decorated and some not. This really happened in בית שאן, and the חכמים said: the decorated shops are forbidden, and the plain ones are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on buying from shops in a city that has עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decorations show that the shop is connected to the idol worship, so buying there is forbidden. Plain shops have no such connection, so they are permitted. The משנה supports its ruling with a real case from בית שאן.

keyTerms.meaning: A city in ארץ ישראל where this case happened

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every shop in the city is forbidden. The משנה forbids only the decorated shops. Plain shops in the same city are permitted.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A city in which there is idol worship,
and there were shops in it that were decorated
and ones that were not decorated —
this was an actual case in Beit She'an,
and the Sages said:
the decorated ones are forbidden,
and those not decorated are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic. It is not connected to the night-water discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Decorated shops in a city with עבודה זרה are forbidden. Plain shops are permitted.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only decorations of roses and myrtle
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש limits the משנה to shops decorated with roses and myrtle. Shops decorated with fruit are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: The משנה forbids only shops decorated with roses and myrtle, because benefit comes from their smell. But shops decorated with fruit are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who narrows the משנה's rule to one kind of decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roses and myrtle give off a smell, so they give benefit right there in the shop. Fruit decorations do not give that kind of benefit while they hang, so those shops are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... This formula limits a rule.
Roses and myrtle, plants with a pleasant smell

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מְעוּטָּרוֹת בְּוֶורֶד וַהֲדַס,
phrases.english: They taught this only about shops decorated with roses and myrtle,
since benefit is gotten from their smell,
but shops decorated with fruit are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which "decorated" shops the משנה means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only shops decorated with sweet-smelling plants are forbidden. Shops decorated with fruit are permitted.

steps.title: Why are fruit decorations permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind ריש לקיש's distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש permits shops decorated with fruit. This sets up the answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit is also an ornament for the idol. So why does it not forbid the shop the way roses do? The גמרא wants the source for the difference.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why shops decorated with fruit are permitted

steps.title: The פסוק: "nothing of the חרם shall stick to your hand"
steps.stepSummary: The reason comes from the פסוק "לא ידבק בידך מאומה מן החרם". It is benefiting from idol items that is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, "Nothing of the banned items shall stick to your hand." It is deriving benefit that is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer with a פסוק. It shows that the problem is getting benefit from items of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that the איסור is about benefiting from idol items. Roses and myrtle give benefit right now through their smell, so that shop is forbidden. The full contrast with fruit continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Banned items, here things devoted to עבודה זרה

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule depends on actual benefit from the idol item, not just on having it in the shop. This idea decides which decorations make a shop forbidden.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"Nothing of the banned items shall stick to your hand,"
it is getting benefit that is forbidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: לֹא יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה מִן הַחֵרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by bringing a פסוק as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק forbids getting benefit from idol items. The smell of roses and myrtle is that kind of benefit.
